now_the_spec_says.THE_DEVICE_TEST_IS_A_PROCESS: A DEVICE IS ITS OWN PROCESS. This is the discriminator the 2026-08-12 axis ruling did not carry, and it is measurable rather than judged: a device runs when nobody called it; a tool and a machine run only when something calls them. It composes with the 2026-08-11 shim rule rather than replacing it — 'a shim FITS TO the device', and the shim is what a process presents to the rack. It also retires 'has a probes/ folder' as the registration path, which is what currently puts cairn/base — the tool drawer — on the device roster.
now_the_spec_says.THE_WHY_IS_A_SURFACE: harbor_master is a device 'So I can see his harbor map.' The why of a device is a LIVED SYMPTOM at a surface, not an architectural property: something must be running for the map to be seeable. This is the operational form of the process test and it is how a borderline case gets decided — ask what a person wants to SEE or SEND TO, not what the code subclasses. It composes with the standing one-web-server rule: a device gets a declared PANE, never its own route, port, or server.
now_the_spec_says.TOOLS_ARE_COMPLETE_PRIMITIVES: A tool is a complete primitive — it holds no parts. A machine is 'groups of tools and glue code to hold them together', so ANYTHING WITH PARTS IS AT LEAST A MACHINE. That test is what demoted Inspector, Learning Block and Gate out of the tools list Akien himself sketched one turn earlier (cairn/tools ...Foo ...Seive ...Inspector ...Gate ...Probe ...Learning Block ...Domain) — the later message supersedes the sketch systematically, and consistently: every composite in that sketch moved up a rung. Domain is the case still unsaid.
now_the_spec_says.A_TOOL_CLASS_BERTHS_AT_THE_DEVICE_CLASS_: cairn/devices/<device>/tools/<tool>/ must exist alongside cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/<tool instance>/. The rule underneath the fix, stated generally: TOOLS BELONG TO A NODE, NOT TO AN INSTANCE. Any node may hold tools, and each level holds only what it adds — which yields a three-level override chain (cairn/tools/Sieve/ definition+defaults -> devices/<d>/tools/Sieve/ this device class's config -> devices/<d>/<i>/tools/Sieve/<name>/ this instance's life). The special-case escape hatch Akien reserved ('my proposal allows special caseing anything if needed') therefore stops being a flag and becomes an override file AT AN ADDRESS, which carries a why for free the way everything at an address does.
now_the_spec_says.CLAUDE_MD_FIRST_PARAGRAPH: RULED CHANGED, and changed this turn. Class-space is no longer described as a flat drawer: it now declares the four rungs, the process test, and that devices/<device>/<instance>/ is ONE ADDRESS WRITTEN IN TWO ROOTS — here the class, the instance's declared config and assembly, and their history; in ~/.cairn/ that same path carrying the instance's life. 'No runtime state here, ever' SURVIVES unchanged, because instance code-and-data and instance runtime-data are two different things and the 2026-08-12 packet already placed the runtime half in .cairn ('the probe's RUNTIME DATA goes in the .cairn tree'). A reader hitting both records will look for a contradiction; there is none, and this clause is why.
now_the_spec_says.THE_SCOPE_IS_RULED_NOT_INFERRED: 'we're reorganizing a lot of bits because the organization didn't fit the map in my head.' The reorganization is the intent, not a side effect of the taxonomy — so its cost is a sequencing question, never a reason to narrow it. Law 9's why: the map in his head is the spec, and cairn/'s flat layout was a translation that lost it.

what_dies: 'has a probes/ folder in class-space' as evidence of device-ness — already killed by the 2026-08-12 packet, now killed a second way: a probes/ folder is not a process.

node_class values of the form 'device (instrument)' where the thing fires only when invoked. cairn/ruling and cairn/orient both carry one and both fail the process test. These are PRE-AXIS vocabulary, written before a device meant a process, and they are the words-kept-meanings-replaced case in its live form: the word 'device' survived while its meaning changed underneath it.

what_conforms: 2026-08-12-tools-machines-devices-instances — the four rungs, the complexity axis, every-device-intends-an-instance, held parts get instance data, machines get a folder alongside tools. This ruling supplies that packet's missing discriminator and its roster.
The 2026-08-11 shim rule ('there is no base device... a shim FITS TO the device') — a shim is what a process presents to the rack, so the process test is what the shim was always testing for.

cairn/orient/ and cairn/chart/orient.py — the tool/machine split is already built and already correctly wired, which is a measurement in the axis's favour: the taxonomy names something already true rather than imposing a shape.
